sources.title: Euryale v2.3 model card and training configuration
sources.evidence: Names L3.3-70B-Euryale-v2.3, explicitly fine-tuned on meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and successor to Euryale v2.2. Dataset labels include roleplay/creative instruction; embedded Axolotl config uses LoRA rank 128 and sequence_len 16384. Card license tag is llama3, not llama3.3. The phrase not Lora-extracted describes its source/training distinction and does not establish full-parameter training. Reopened pinned and current cards October 27; they are byte-identical. Both metadata and training config explicitly name meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. No pruning, distillation, expert expansion, added modality or architectural resizing is described.

sources.title: Euryale v2.3 checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: LlamaForCausalLM, 80 layers, hidden size 8192, intermediate size 28672, vocabulary 128256, 64 attention heads, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128; attention_bias and mlp_bias false, tie_word_embeddings false, BF16, max_position_embeddings 131072, Llama-3 RoPE scaling factor 8, Transformers 4.46.3. No quantization or custom architecture configuration. Reopened October 27; current config is byte-identical to this pinned revision and retains the named Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct path and ordinary Llama dimensions.

sources.title: Complete Euryale v2.3 checkpoint index and all 30 bounded tensor headers
sources.evidence: Original audit independently fetched the 8-byte prefix and JSON header of every one of the 30 indexed safetensors shards at this revision, verifying HTTP 206 and exact Content-Range. Only 84,880 prefix/header bytes were fetched, no weight data. All 723 distinct indexed BF16 tensors match their shard assignment and expected enabled-module shapes; byte ranges are contiguous/non-overlapping and cover each shard payload. Sum is 70,553,706,496 learned elements, consistent with index total_size 141,107,412,992 bytes. These are complete merged model tensors, not an adapter-only checkpoint. October 27 parameter re-audit refetched only this index: its 723 names exactly match the configured Llama modules, with no residual adapters or extra structural modules; total_size is unchanged. No shard or shard header was fetched during the re-audit.

sources.title: Enabled LlamaForCausalLM implementation at Transformers 4.46.3
sources.evidence: LlamaForCausalLM enables a token embedding, 80 LlamaDecoderLayer modules and final RMSNorm, plus bias-free LM head. Attention and MLP biases follow false config flags. RMSNorm has a learned scale; rotary inv_freq is a nonpersistent buffer. Config-selected causal LM does not instantiate sequence/token classification or question-answering heads. No routed experts, extra MTP head, external draft model or learned rotary parameter is present. Reopened this exact implementation October 27 and reconciled the enabled embedding, untied output head, attention/MLP dimensions and RMSNorm parameters with current creator config and index.

sources.title: Euryale v2.3 tokenizer and shipped chat template
sources.evidence: Text tokenizer has model_max_length 131072. The shipped template accepts tools/custom_tools, prompts the model to select a function with JSON name and parameters, serializes assistant tool_calls, handles tool/ipython results, and explicitly restricts to one tool call at a time. This is positive model-side function-call formatting support; it is not a claim of benchmark reliability or execution inside the model. No dedicated reasoning/thinking switch or reasoning output channel is documented.

sources.title: Phi-4: Microsoft Research January 2025 brief, page 1
sources.evidence: Reopened the original two-page PDF October 27 and independently visually inspected page 1. The comparison plot explicitly labels the horizontal axis Active Parameters (Billions) and places Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct at approximately 70B. This is Microsoft Research's published nominal active-count convention for the exact named Euryale base, not an active disclosure by Meta or Sao10K, and does not establish an exact per-token tensor census.

sources.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents, Figure 11
sources.publisher: Kale-ab Abebe Tessera et al.; University of Edinburgh, University of Oxford and University College London
sources.evidence: Reopened the original June 2026 paper October 27 and independently visually inspected Figure 11 on PDF page 24. The horizontal axis is explicitly Active parameters (billions, log scale), with Llama 3.3 70B at approximately 70B. Section 4.1 and Table 1 identify the evaluated model as Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, served with vLLM. This later original benchmark corroborates the nominal active convention for the exact base, without providing a separately measured count for Euryale or exact per-token participation.

parameters_b.note: Retain exact complete checkpoint count 70,553,706,496 learned parameters from the original 723-tensor BF16 header audit. Fresh October 27 creator card/config, index and enabled implementation checks reproduce 2*128256*8192 + 80*(2*8192*8192 + 2*8192*1024 + 3*8192*28672 + 2*8192) + 8192, and current Hugging Face metadata independently matches. Includes distinct input embedding and untied output head, attention/MLP matrices and RMSNorm scales. The creator explicitly fine-tuned Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct with LoRA; complete merged weights retain its dimensions with no residual adapters, pruning, added experts or modality modules. No shard was downloaded in this re-audit.

active_parameters_b.note: Approximately 70B nominal active parameters, inferred through the creator's explicitly named Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct lineage and unchanged merged Llama structure. Microsoft Research's original January 2025 comparison plot puts that exact base at approximately 70B on its Active Parameters axis; the June 2026 ALEM original benchmark corroborates the convention. Euryale's LoRA training is merged into the ordinary complete checkpoint, with no structural change found. This is an attributed research-comparison convention transferred through documented lineage, not a separate Sao10K disclosure, exact per-token count, or equality with the precise 70.553706496B total.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Llama Transformer with 80 layers, grouped-query attention (64 query/8 KV heads), SwiGLU MLPs, RMSNorm and RoPE. Every layer has ordinary attention/MLP matrices; no expert router. Configuration and complete checkpoint agree.

context_window.note: Model config and tokenizer both specify 131072; author explicitly confirms 128k while recommending up to 32k. Training sequence_len 16384 and an individual hosted endpoint limit are different quantities; no claim of equal quality at every context length.

modalities.note: Text token inputs and causal vocabulary logits; complete checkpoint contains no vision/audio encoder or projection modules.

reasoning.note: Primary exact-model material does not establish a dedicated reasoning/thinking mode or an explicit negative. Ordinary instruction following and later Vulpecula reasoning-trace training are not evidence of Euryale thinking support. Clear baseline false.

tool_call.note: Exact shipped template positively implements model-selected single function calls with JSON arguments, assistant tool_calls and returned tool messages. This establishes supported calling format, not measured fine-tune reliability or execution by the model. Clear baseline false; do not substitute a provider tools listing for the checkpoint template.

patch.license: Llama 3 Community License (card); Llama 3.3 Community License (base)
patch.description: Sao10K's Llama 3.3 70B Instruct fine-tune for roleplay and creative text generation.
patch.notes: Euryale v2.3 has 70.553706496B total parameters in its complete merged BF16 checkpoint. Approximately 70B active follows Microsoft Research's published convention for its explicitly named Llama 3.3 70B Instruct base, corroborated by the later ALEM benchmark and inherited through unchanged model structure; it is not an exact per-token count or a separate Sao10K disclosure. Complete weights were uploaded December 7, 2024 and publicly discussed by December 8; first public day is unresolved, so release uses month precision rather than the later December 18 provider date. Author card labels llama3 although its explicit Llama 3.3 base uses Llama 3.3 Community License; this license-version discrepancy is preserved. Model/tokenizer context is 131072; author recommends up to 32k and training used 16384-token sequences. The shipped template supports single function calls; no dedicated reasoning mode is documented. Training config uses LoRA, but the distributed checkpoint is complete merged model weights.

Resolve active parameters to approximately 70B under Microsoft Research's original comparison-plot convention, corroborated by ALEM Figure 11 and inherited through the explicitly named Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct LoRA lineage without structural changes.
